newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Shipping to save from Australia levy cut - minister.
newsitem.headline: Shipping to save from Australia levy cut - minister.

text.p: Australian Transport Minister John Sharp said on Wednesday an annual saving of A$3.5 million was expected to flow to the shipping industry following a reduction in the Australian Maritime Safety Authority's levies.
Sharp said the marine navigation levy rate for all vessels over 20,000 tonnes would be halved, while the rate for vessels of less than 20,000 tonnes would remain unchanged.

"This significant reduction in charges on the shipping industry is in line with AMSA's objective of enhancing efficiency while delivering a high standard of safety and other services to the maritime industry," Sharp said in a statement.
The proposed new levy rates, operational from July 1, were the result of a continuing improvement in AMSA's operational management and financial performance, Sharp said.

The marine navigation levy is charged to commercial trading ships using Australian ports to recover the cost of providing safety and navigational services, including lighthouses and advanced technology electronic navigation systems.
